conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: A surfaces the decisive uncertainty in the grid itself: a Production-critical column reading 'Unconfirmed' on every initial record, so a reviewer can separate stale candidates from possibly-critical production connections before selecting anything. Both builds write good confirmation copy, but in B every dialog's primary/destructive confirm button renders white-on-white (measured contrast 1.00 for 'Disable 2 connections', 1.56 for 'Delete permanently'), so the only control that completes the required bulk action is an apparently blank box — reproduced live and visible in B's own error-state screenshot. A also keeps Delete inside a per-row overflow menu behind a disabled typed-count confirm, while B puts a red Delete link on every row, closer to a casual default. A's inspectable accessibility is stronger too: real table with scope='col' headers, two aria-live regions, and focus-visible styles, versus B's div role='table', no live regions, and no focus styles anywhere in its CSS.
suspected_unblinding: none — the two differ in theme and stack idiom, but nothing identified a treatment or builder

unsupported_claims.label: B
unsupported_claims.claim: Bulk-disable failure reason asserts a policy the scenario never supplies — that a record with no owner must have an owner assigned before it can be disabled.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The primary confirm button in the bulk-disable dialog is white text on a white background, so its label is invisible and the only control that completes the required bulk action reads as an empty box.
findings.evidence: Reproduced locally (served B/source on a local port, driven with a local Playwright chromium): computed color rgb(255,255,255) on background rgb(255,255,255), contrast ratio 1.00. Cause is `.dialog-actions button { background:#fff }` overriding `.btn-primary` background while `.btn-primary { color:#fff }` still applies (B/source/styles.css lines 117 and 350). Also visible in B/evidence/interaction-03-bulk-disable-with-confirmation.png.

findings.label: B
findings.description: The same defect hits the destructive path and the result dialog: 'Delete permanently' measures 1.56 contrast and the bulk-result dismiss button renders as a blank white rectangle.
findings.evidence: Reproduced locally: delete dialog button computed color rgb(255,255,255) on rgb(230,200,198). Blank dismiss control shown in B/evidence/state-03-bulk-action-error-for-one-selected-record.png.

findings.label: B
findings.description: No aria-live or status region exists anywhere, so filter counts and bulk-disable results are not announced, and Escape does not dismiss the modal.
findings.evidence: Reproduced locally: querySelectorAll('[aria-live],[role=status],[role=alert]') returns 0 elements; after pressing Escape with the bulk dialog open, the [role=alertdialog] node is still in the DOM. A returns two aria-live='polite' regions and closes on Escape.

findings.label: B
findings.description: Production-critical status — the field the brief says must be inspected before bulk action — is absent from the table and appears only after opening a record's detail modal.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png shows columns Application, Owner, Environment, Scopes, Last used, Token expiry, Status, Actions; the 'Not specified — verify before disabling or deleting' line appears only in B/evidence/interaction-02-inspect-one-record.png.

findings.label: B
findings.description: A red Delete link sits on every row beside View and Disable, presenting the irreversible action at the same level of casualness as the reversible one.
findings.evidence: B/desktop.png — Actions column repeats 'View Disable Delete' on all ten rows; A places Delete inside a per-row overflow menu (A/evidence/interaction-02-inspect-one-record.png).

findings.label: B
findings.description: The grid is a div with role='table' whose column headers carry no scope, and the select-all header cell has no accessible name.
findings.evidence: Reproduced locally: 0 <table> elements, one DIV[role=table]; first [role=columnheader] has empty text content. A exposes a real <table> with ten scope='col' headers.

findings.label: A
findings.description: At 390 px, label and value collide in the card layout so metadata reads as run-together text.
findings.evidence: A/mobile.png — 'Last usedNever used', 'ExpiresIn 96 days', 'ExpiresIn 24 days' on successive cards.

findings.label: A
findings.description: Modal dialogs omit aria-modal and do not move focus into the dialog when opened, so a keyboard or screen-reader user stays behind the overlay.
findings.evidence: Reproduced locally: bulk confirm dialog has role='alertdialog' and aria-labelledby but aria-modal is null and document.activeElement is outside the dialog after it opens. (B shares the focus-placement problem but does set aria-modal='true'.)

findings.label: A
findings.description: Some generated rows assert a definite 'Not critical' production-critical value rather than marking the field unknown, which reads as data the scenario never supplied; B labels its generated rows 'placeholder' more honestly.
findings.evidence: A/desktop.png — Password Rotator and Session Logger show 'Not critical' while the initial records correctly show 'Unconfirmed'; B/desktop.png tags fabricated rows with a 'placeholder' chip.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The detail side panel overlaps the right edge of the table and clips the Production-critical column of the row being inspected.
findings.evidence: A/evidence/interaction-02-inspect-one-record.png — the row's badge is cut to 'Unconfir…' behind the panel.
